parts:
This looks like an unrotated EFA model. In that case, ALL covariances
among the latent variables should be zero. Try

fit <- sem(mymodel, data = mydat, orthogonal = TRUE)

Yves.

On 11/10/23 03:58, 'alexande...@yahoo.com' via lavaan wrote:
> Hello, I am currently trying to fit a Structural Equation Model using
> lavaan to data that I have simulated, and am having issues with model
> convergence. I have attached a png of the path diagram for the model to
> this discussion. Forgive me if it is slightly hard to read, I was not
> very familiar with the software I used to generate it. My goal in
> fitting this model is to estimate the factor loading matrices. I want to
> accurately estimate the factor loading matrices (which are known as I
> use them to simulate the data), and to do so, I impose several
> constraints such that there is no indeterminancy (rotational, scalar, or
> otherwise). The constraints, as seen in the path diagram, are as follows:
>
> 1. For the factor loadings between my observed independent covariates
> (X1-X20) and the latent factors from which they are generated (W1-W3), I
> have fixed the factor loadings for X1~W1, X2~W2, and X3~W3 at 1, and the
> factor loadings for X1~W2, X1~W3, and X2~W3 at 0.
>
> 2. For the factor loadings between my observed dependent covariates
> (Y1-Y20) and the latent factors from which they are generated (Z1-Z2), I
> have fixed the factor loadings for Y1~Z1, and Y2~Z2 at 1, and the factor
> loading for Y1~Z2 at 0.
>
> 3. The 3 latent factors W1, W2, and W3 have variance 1, and all 3 are
> mutually independent.
>
> To the best of my knowledge, these should be sufficient conditions such
> that the remaining (unfixed) factor loadings between (X1-X20) and
> (W1-W3), (Y1-Y20) and (Z1-Z2), and coefficient matrix containing the
> regression estimates of (Z1-Z2) on (W1-W3) can all be uniquely
> estimated. Of course, the true factor loadings and covariance matrix of
> (W1-W3) are correspondingly fixed at these values. The covariance
> matrices of the error terms (which are simply the identity matrix)
> should be estimable as well, though these are not of particular interest
> currently. However, when I try and fit this model as I have defined it
> in lavaan, I receive a warning message from the optimizer stating that a
> solution has not been found, and correspondingly, the estimated factor
> loadings and regression coefficients are quite inaccurate. I have found
> that when I fix a single one of the regression coefficients of (Z1-Z2)
> on (W1-W3) at the truth (it does not seem to matter which coefficient I
> choose), I receive no warnings or errors when fitting the model, and the
> estimated factor loadings and regression coefficients are accurate. Is
> anyone able to help me figure out why these issues are arising when
> fitting the model? I have also included below the R code I have used to
> define and fit my model. Please let me know if any further
> clarifications are desired. Thank you very much for the assistance.
>
> Best,
>
> Alexander
>
>
>
>

>   }

>     W <- matrix(rnorm(n*ncol(gamma), mean = 0, sd = 1), nrow =
> ncol(gamma), n) ## generate matrix U N(0,I) m x n
>   }
>   xlin.term  <-  bk %*% rbind(rep(1, ncol(W)),W)
>   xlin.term <- t(xlin.term)
>   xx <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = nrow(bk))
>   for(jj in 1: (ncol(xx))){
>     xx[, jj] <- xlin.term[,jj] + cbind(rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd =
> sqrt(varvecB[jj])))
>   }
>   colnames(xlin.term) <- paste0('X', 1:(ncol(xx)))

>     Z <- matrix(0, nrow=nrow(gamma), ncol = n)
